newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt warns mine bosses to curb pollution.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt warns mine bosses to curb pollution.

text.p: South Africa's Water Affairs Minister, Kader Asmal, told the mining industry on Monday to spend more of its profits on limiting pollution.

"The cost of pollution is high to the taxpayer. It is time that the mines take responsibility for rehabilitating the environment," he said at the official opening of a 26 million rand water pollution control works in Mpumalanga province.

Asmal said the industry should tackle the rehabilitation of mines as an integral part of mining operations, recovering the cost from mineral sales. There would no longer be any "easy rides" for the industry's financial obligations to the environment, he added.

"Mine(owners) should come up front to address the life cycle of the mines. They must have enough funds to rehabilitate the environment. The money generated should then be used for catchment management," the minister said.

Asmal announced he would immediately start an investigation with the Department of Mineral and Energy Affairs into the remedial measures necessary to stop slimes dams from polluting underground water.
If serious breaches of the Water Act were uncovered, prosecution would follow, he warned.
